signals.title: AUD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Fed-RBA Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags USD outperformance at +1.150% across 9 pairs against AUD underperformance at -1.827% across 4 pairs, creating a 2.977% bilateral spread. AUD/USD trades at 0.6658, holding well below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.6904/0.6975/0.7050 with trend structure confirming an active downtrend extended 5.09 ATR below the 20-day average. The broader move reflects surging US real yields alongside Fed hawkishness, reinforced by J.P. Morgan and Barclays revising calls to multiple upcoming rate hikes. Although RBA at 4.85% maintains an 85bp nominal policy rate premium over the Fed at 4.00%, Australia's softer October employment decline of 43,500 and negative ESI of -6.9 erode domestic support. Retail sentiment sits at an extreme 87% long, setting up sharp unwind vulnerability against the prevailing trend. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, downtrend acceleration with retail capitulation risk. Catalyst: Fed Governor Waller speech at 13:25 UTC. Risk: Sharp risk-asset rebound that compresses the bilateral G10 spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium + Technical Barrier
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.73, holding above its SMA20/50/200 moving-average cluster at 158.53/157.85/158.73. A 275bp policy rate advantage for the Fed at 4.00% versus the BoJ at 1.25%, backed by a 267bp OIS SOFR-TONA spread, sustains persistent upside demand. The 160.00 threshold remains the key level that has previously triggered Ministry of Finance verbal warnings and intervention scrutiny. Elevated cross-asset volatility with VIX at 28.4 introduces headline sensitivity, while 25d risk reversals at -1.41 reflect persistent institutional hedging against abrupt downside gaps. The correlation between USD/JPY and VIX sits at +0.010 versus the 252-day norm of +0.275 (z = -2.00σ), confirming typical safe-haven mechanics remain distorted by strong US yield support. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported while holding below official intervention thresholds. Catalyst: Japan Core CPI release follow-through and US Michigan Inflation Expectations at 15:00 UTC. Risk: Physical FX intervention by Japanese authorities on a sustained print above 160.00.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short + Policy Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.0972, positioned below its SMA20/50/200 moving averages at 1.1127/1.1246/1.1514 in an established downtrend extended 2.49 ATR below the 20-day mean. CFTC data indicates Leveraged Funds hold net short positions of -98,604 contracts, placing positioning at the 6th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of -1.58. The policy rate spread of 135bp between Fed at 4.00% and ECB at 2.65% favors USD, with SOFR trading 146bp above €STR. US 5Y yields rose 23bp over the last 5 sessions, driven almost entirely by real yields (+22bp vs +1bp breakeven, FRED, as of Nov 17), expanding the trans-Atlantic real yield gap. Retail sentiment shows 85% long positioning, directly opposing the institutional net short and warning of further downside pressure if retail stops trigger. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, structural policy and real yield divergence dominant. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde speech at 08:30 UTC. Risk: Leveraged Funds short-covering squeeze reclaiming the SMA20 at 1.1127.

signals.title: EUR/JPY — Risk Reversal Put Skew + Downside Hedging
signals.text: EUR/JPY trades at 175.19, supported by a 140bp rate spread between the ECB at 2.65% and the BoJ at 1.25%, with the OIS €STR-TONA differential at 122bp. The 1M 25-delta risk reversal sits at -1.58, indicating strong put skew and heavy institutional demand for downside tail protection. This aggressive downside options pricing emerges alongside broader equity market weakness, with S&P 500 falling 2.02% and VIX rising to 28.4. While carry flows keep spot elevated, the options market is pricing sharp asymmetry should risk liquidation accelerate into the weekend. The BEER fair value model shows cross-currency misalignment with high implied volatility across European assets. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/JPY on cross-asset de-risking, options skew pricing downside shock. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde speech at 08:30 UTC. Risk: Broader equity market stabilization lowering VIX back below 20.0.
